text:
maya: Quick follow-up on the admission-smoothing RFC — thinking about edge cases for cross-tenant fairness when we redispatch credits during failover. Specifically: if a Dedicated pool fails over to shared, how do we avoid starving low-priority tenants while still honoring reserved capacity? Anyone seen sims for 'graceful handoff' shape?

trevor: short answer: cap the borrow rate + keep a small per-tenant floor. we prototyped something similar in staging last month.

john: +1. also add a probation flag so newly-borrowed credits are subject to softer burst limits for N minutes to prevent oscillation.

nina: curious about observability — we need token provenance in traces. if credits are reissued from different pools we should tag spans with origin pool and admit_reason.

ops-bot: reminder: rollout checklist for redispatch landing: canary 1 -> 5% -> 20% with circuit monitor.

leo: thought: what about abuse signals? If a tenant suddenly uses redispatched credits at high qps we should trigger a temporary weight decay instead of hard eviction. less noisy for downstream.

maya: sounds good — tradeoffs: floor prevents total starvation but increases worst-case latency for high-priority traffic; probation prevents abuse but reduces responsiveness for legitimate bursts. propose an interface:

``
admit_request { tenant_id, requested_tokens, pool_origin, probation: bool }
admit_response { granted_tokens, source_pool, probation_window_seconds }
```

maya: Any objections to adding 'probation' to the admission API and plumbing origin metadata into tracing? If not I'll add a short RFC follow-up with metrics to capture (per-tenant floor hits, probation_grants, origin-switch-rate).

trevor: +1 from infra. please include SLI for 're-dispatch-induced latency' and a plan for tuning floors per customer class.

john: +1 security — add an abuse heuristic: if origin-switch-rate > X && high qps => temp weight_decay.

nina: i'll sketch the dash tiles for provenance and probation exposures.

maya: great — i'll open the follow-up and tag people. :thumbsup:
